hints.reason: Bills per-vCore-hour, not a flat SKU rate. IMPORTANT: this productName family exposes ~18 rows, one per fixed vCore-count SKU (skuName '1 vCore', '4 vCore', ..., '80 vCore', plus Zone Redundancy variants) that are each ALREADY pre-multiplied by their vCore count (e.g. '4 vCore' = $0.669756 = 4 x $0.167439) — matching on 'meterNameContains: vCore' alone (a first run's mistake) pulls in all of them plus the true per-unit rate, and multiplying an already-multiplied row by this hint's own quantityJsonPath would double- or quadruple-count. skuNameEquals 'vCore' (exact, not contains) isolates just the single true per-vCore-hour base rate row (skuName literally 'vCore', armSkuName 'SQLMI_GP_Compute_Gen5'); meterNameEquals 'vCore' excludes the separate 'Zone Redundancy vCore' meter. Confirmed via Azure Retail Prices API, westeurope: $0.167439/vCore-hour. At this catalog's 4-vCore requestBody (also Azure's own real floor for General Purpose), that's 4 x $0.167439 = $0.669756/hour. Also see https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/pricing/details/azure-sql-managed-instance/single/ for the billing-granularity quote already in this catalog's notes.

$3.20/hour for the Standard_B1 SKU (source: Azure Retail Prices API and https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/pricing/details/key-vault/, verified this session). Manual rate used because the exact meterName string for this meter wasn't captured verbatim during that research pass — re-derive live serviceName/meterNameContains next time this hint is revisited rather than trusting this fixed number indefinitely. Only one SKU exists for Managed HSM (no smaller option), so minimumUnits is 1 pool.

Multi-VM cluster (2x Standard_D3_v2 head + 1x Standard_D3_v2 worker + 3x Standard_A4_v2 zookeeper nodes) — no single Retail Prices API meter represents this; it's a sum across 6 VM instances of 2 different sizes. Confirmed rates this session: D3_v2 ~$0.29/hour, D1_v2 ~$0.07/hour (A4_v2's exact rate wasn't separately confirmed). $1.25/hour is a midpoint estimate within the ~$1-1.50/hour range this session computed for the 6-node layout, NOT independently re-verified per-node — lowest-confidence entry in this catalog's cost data alongside the two ServiceFabric cluster types. Billing is genuinely per-minute (quoted verbatim from Microsoft: "We charge for the number of minutes your cluster is running, rounded to the nearest minute, not hour"), so a brief test costs less than a full hour's worth.

$1.0081/hour for the A1 SKU (source: Azure Retail Prices API and https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/pricing/details/power-bi-embedded/, verified this session). Confirmed genuine per-second proration despite hourly-rate framing — quoted verbatim: "Actual usage is computed to the second and billed hourly." A1 is the smallest available capacity SKU, hence minimumUnits 1.

$1.51/hour for the DW100c SKU (source: Azure Retail Prices API and https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/pricing/details/synapse-analytics/, verified this session — corrected the meterNameContains after a first run found zero matches: the real meterName is the generic '100 DWUs' for every performance tier of this product, with the actual tier disambiguated only by skuName, e.g. 'DW100c'/'DW200c'/.../'DW30000c', all sharing that same meterName). Confirmed hourly-minimum billing (no sub-hour proration), quoted verbatim: "If your data warehouse exists for only 30 minutes in a month, you will be billed for 1 hour." DW100c is the smallest performance level Synapse dedicated SQL pools offer, hence minimumUnits 1 (sold as a fixed named tier, not linearly per-DWU).

$0.31/hour for the Premium tier, 4 vCore SKU (source: Azure Retail Prices API and https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/pricing/details/database-migration/, verified this session — meaningfully cheaper than an earlier unverified guess of $0.84-1.68/hour). This is a flat named-SKU meter (the '4 vCore' qualifier is baked into the meter itself, like Synapse's DW100c or PowerBI's A1), NOT a per-vCore-hour linear rate — deliberately no quantityJsonPath/minimumUnits here, since multiplying $0.31 by a vCore count would quadruple it incorrectly. Microsoft's pricing page states the first 6 months of 4-vCore Premium usage is free per subscription from service creation, so a brief first-time test may show $0 — not reflected in this static rate. Billing granularity (hourly-minimum vs. prorated) not explicitly confirmed; treat $0.31 as a per-hour-or-less ceiling.
